lines.text: 3.1.2 Food also varies from time to time
Food varies across the map. Does it also vary across the years?
Ask the oldest person you can reach, and you will find that it does —
not just the dishes, but the whole business of cooking. The tools
have changed, the fuel has changed, the time it takes has changed.
ACTIVITY
Activity 3.3 — Interview an elder
Choose someone at least fifty years older than you —
a grandparent, a neighbour, a retired teacher.
Prepare your questions before you meet them. Write them down.
Good starting points:
What did you eat as a child that you still eat today?
What did you eat then that you never eat now?
• How was the food cooked, and on what?
• How long did the cooking take?
What changed, and when did it change?
Listen more than you talk. Write their answers in their words, not yours.
Bring your notes to class and pool them with your classmates'.
